examples.en: My mother does gardening as a hobby.

examples.ko: 원예 용품은 꽃집이나 마트에서 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy gardening supplies at a flower shop or a supermarket.
I got interested in gardening and bought a flower pot.

examples.ko: 원예가 취미인 분이 많아서 주말 농장이 인기예요.
examples.en: Many people enjoy gardening, so weekend farms are popular.

examples.ko: 베란다에서 하는 원예는 작은 공간에서도 가능해요.
examples.en: Gardening on a balcony is possible even in a small space.
This university has a horticulture department.

explain: '농사'보다 꽃·채소·화분을 가꾸는 취미의 느낌이 강해요. '원예 용품', '원예 치료'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 많이 써요. 집 마당이나 베란다에서 식물을 키우는 이야기에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The hospital held a horticultural therapy class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물을 키우면서 마음을 편하게 하는 활동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to calming the mind by growing plants.

phrases.en: Gardening is my hobby these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물 가꾸기를 취미로 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural for describing plant care as a hobby.

phrases.en: I learn gardening at the culture center every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이나 화분 가꾸는 방법을 공부할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when studying how to care for flowers and pots.

explain_en: Compared with '농사' (farming), it has a stronger feeling of a hobby of tending flowers, vegetables and potted plants. It often comes before another noun, as in '원예 용품' and '원예 치료'. It suits talk about growing plants in a yard or on a balcony.

en: to rest; to get away; to relax

examples.ko: 의사가 한 달 동안 시골에서 휴양하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to rest in the countryside for a month.
He read books while relaxing at the beach.
My hobby is getting away to the mountains every weekend.
I rested at home until my body recovered.
The hotel is full of people who came to relax.
This summer I'm going to relax on Jeju Island.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '쉬다', '푹 쉬다'가 훨씬 흔해요. '휴양하다'는 병이나 피로를 회복하려고 쉴 때, 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. '휴양지에서 휴양하다'는 말이 겹치니 '휴양지에서 쉬다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I rested well at home on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '휴양하다'보다 이 말이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk this is much more natural than 휴양하다.

phrases.en: Grandmother went to the seaside to recuperate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬는 것이 목적인 여행을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a trip whose purpose is rest.

phrases.example: 아버지는 병 때문에 시골에서 휴양하고 있어요.
phrases.en: My father is recuperating in the countryside because of an illness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 피로를 풀려고 쉬는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means resting to recover from illness or fatigue.

explain_en: Resting away from home to recover, such as countryside. In daily talk '쉬다' or '푹 쉬다' is much more common. '휴양하다' shows up more in writing and news, for resting to recover from illness or fatigue. '휴양지에서 휴양하다' repeats itself, so '휴양지에서 쉬다' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: I rested at home until my body recovered.

examples.en: There is an old zelkova tree at the entrance of the village.
In summer we rest in the shade of the zelkova tree.
Grandfather plays Korean chess under the zelkova tree.
The leaves of a zelkova tree turn yellow in autumn.

examples.ko: 천 년 된 느티나무를 보러 시골에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the countryside to see a thousand-year-old zelkova tree.
The kids played climbing the zelkova tree.

explain: 한국 시골 마을 입구에서 자주 보는 큰 나무예요. 그늘이 넓어서 사람들이 모여 쉬는 곳이 되고, 오래된 느티나무는 마을을 지키는 '당산나무'로 여겨지기도 해요. '소나무', '은행나무'처럼 나무 이름에는 '-나무'가 붙어요.

phrases.en: The grandmothers are sitting in the shade of the zelkova tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여름에 쉬거나 모이는 자리를 말할 때 '느티나무'와 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the shady spot where people rest or gather in summer.

phrases.en: I'm meeting my friend under the zelkova tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소나 쉬는 곳을 말할 때 쓰는 위치 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A location phrase used for meeting spots or resting places.

phrases.example: 학교 앞에 큰 느티나무가 한 그루 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a big zelkova tree in front of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 느티나무는 크게 자라서 '큰'과 같이 말하면 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Zelkova trees grow large, so 'big' pairs naturally with it.

explain_en: It is a big tree often seen at the entrance of Korean country villages. Its wide shade becomes a resting place, and old ones are sometimes treated as a village guardian tree, a '당산나무'. Tree names take '-나무', as in '소나무' and '은행나무'.

examples.en: Grandma feeds the chickens in the yard.
Every morning pigeons come to eat the feed.

examples.ko: 새장 속의 새가 모이를 다 먹었어요.
examples.en: The bird in the cage ate all of its feed.

examples.ko: 공원에는 모이 주기를 금지한다는 표지판이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a sign in the park that says feeding the birds is banned.

examples.ko: 병아리는 작은 모이도 열심히 쪼아 먹어요.
examples.en: Chicks eagerly peck at even small bits of feed.
The kids bought feed to give to the ducks.

explain: 모이는 새나 닭처럼 작은 동물에게 주는 먹이만 가리켜요. 개나 고양이 먹이는 '사료'라고 하고, '모이를 주다', '모이를 쪼다'처럼 써요. 같은 소리의 '모이다(함께 모이다)'와는 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I feed the chickens every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새나 닭에게 먹이를 줄 때 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for feeding birds or chickens.

phrases.en: A sparrow is pecking at feed in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새가 부리로 먹이를 먹는 모습을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a bird eating with its beak.

phrases.en: Grandfather scatters feed in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 마리에게 한꺼번에 먹이를 흩어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when scattering feed for many animals at once.

explain_en: Food for birds or poultry (비둘기) '모이' is only for the food you give to small animals like birds and chickens. Food for dogs and cats is '사료'. You say '모이를 주다' (give feed) or '모이를 쪼다' (peck at feed). It has nothing to do with the verb '모이다' (to gather).

examples.en: I saw a polar bear for the first time at the zoo.
Polar bears live on the ice.

examples.ko: 얼음이 녹아서 북극곰이 살 곳이 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: The ice is melting, so the places polar bears can live are shrinking.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 북극곰 인형을 안고 자요.
examples.en: My child sleeps hugging a polar bear doll.
I watched a video of a polar bear swimming underwater.

examples.ko: 흰 털 때문에 북극곰은 눈 속에서 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: Because of its white fur, a polar bear is hard to see in the snow.

explain: 곰 이름은 사는 곳이나 모습을 붙인 것이 많아요. '불곰', '반달가슴곰'처럼요. 북극곰은 지구 온난화 이야기가 나올 때 환경 뉴스에 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: I got a polar bear doll as a birthday gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북극곰 모양의 인형을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a stuffed toy shaped like a polar bear.

phrases.en: A polar bear swims in the cold sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북극곰의 모습을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common verb for describing what polar bears do.

phrases.en: There is a polar bear family in the photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 엄마 곰과 새끼 곰처럼 함께 있는 북극곰을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for polar bears together, like a mother and cubs.

explain_en: Many bear names add where they live or how they look, like '불곰' (brown bear) and '반달가슴곰' (Asian black bear). '북극곰' often appears in environment news about global warming.

examples.en: I reread the report and revised it.
Please correct the wrong parts.
How about revising the plan a little?
I touched up the photo's colors and then posted it.

examples.ko: 한 번 보낸 글은 수정할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't edit a post once it's sent.
I wrote the name wrong, so I came to fix it.

explain: 글, 계획, 사진처럼 이미 있는 것을 조금 고칠 때 써요. '고치다'는 고장 난 물건에도 쓰지만 수정하다는 문서나 내용에 더 잘 어울려요. '바로잡다'는 틀린 것을 맞게 한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I fixed the wrong letters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고장 난 물건에도 쓰는 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that also works for broken things.

phrases.en: I corrected the wrong content.
phrases.nuance_ko: 틀린 것을 맞게 한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a stronger sense of making wrong things right.

phrases.en: The plan was revised a little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고쳐지는 대상이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the thing being revised is the subject.

explain_en: Use it for adjusting something that already exists, such as a text, plan, or photo. 고치다 also covers fixing broken objects, but 수정하다 fits documents and content better. 바로잡다 leans more toward making a mistake right.

examples.en: Palm trees stand in a row along the beach.
I rested for a while in the shade of a palm tree.

examples.ko: 야자나무 열매로 만든 주스를 마셔 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried juice made from palm tree fruit.

examples.ko: 이 호텔 정원에는 야자나무를 열 그루쯤 심었어요.
examples.en: They planted about ten palm trees in this hotel's garden.

examples.ko: 바람에 흔들리는 야자나무 사진이 제 배경 화면이에요.
examples.en: A photo of a palm tree swaying in the wind is my wallpaper.

examples.ko: 야자나무는 추운 곳에서는 잘 자라지 못해요.
examples.en: Palm trees can't grow well in cold places.

explain: '야자수'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 휴양지 풍경을 말할 때는 둘 다 자주 나와요. 우리가 흔히 먹고 마시는 '코코넛'은 이 나무의 열매 중 하나예요.

phrases.en: I rested under the palm trees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같은 말이고 휴양지 풍경에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word with the same meaning, often used for resort scenery.

phrases.en: I picked a palm tree fruit and tried it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무의 열매를 말할 때 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the fruit of the tree.

phrases.en: I walked slowly through the palm tree forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무가 많은 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a place with many palm trees.

explain_en: '야자수' is used in a similar way, and both words come up when describing resort scenery. The '코코넛' (coconut) we often eat and drink is one of the fruits of this kind of tree.

t90.ax: I tried juice made from palm tree fruit.

examples.en: The probe arrived safely on Mars.

examples.ko: 달 탐사선 발사 장면을 생중계로 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the lunar probe launch live.

examples.ko: 탐사선은 멀리서 사진을 찍어 보내 줘요.
examples.en: The probe takes pictures from far away and sends them.

examples.ko: 이 탐사선은 십 년 넘게 우주를 날고 있어요.
examples.en: This probe has been flying through space for over ten years.
In science class, we made a model of a space probe.

examples.ko: 새 탐사선 덕분에 목성의 모습이 더 자세히 알려졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the new probe, Jupiter's appearance is known in more detail.

explain: 사람이 타는 것은 '우주선', 사람 없이 먼 곳을 조사하러 보내는 것은 탐사선이에요. 앞에 '화성', '달'처럼 목적지를 붙여 말해요. 뉴스와 과학 시간에 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The Mars probe sent back photos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 목적지를 붙여 어디를 조사하는 탐사선인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the destination in front to say where the probe explores.

phrases.en: Scientists sent a probe to Jupiter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼 곳을 조사하려고 탐사선을 우주로 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for sending a probe to space to study a faraway place.

phrases.en: An unmanned probe has no people aboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 타지 않는다는 점을 분명히 할 때 '무인'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Unmanned' stresses that no people are on board.

explain_en: A craft that carries people is a 우주선, while one sent without people to study a distant place is a 탐사선. Put the destination before it, as in 화성 or 달 탐사선. It often appears in news and science class.

examples.en: A panorama of the city spread out from the observatory.
I took a panorama photo with my phone.

examples.ko: 산 정상에서 본 파노라마가 정말 멋졌어요.
examples.en: The panorama from the summit was really beautiful.

examples.ko: 파노라마 창문 덕분에 바다가 다 보여요.
examples.en: Thanks to the panoramic window, I can see the whole sea.
I previewed the destination in a panoramic video.

examples.ko: 카페에서 한강 파노라마를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see a panorama of the Han River from the cafe.

explain: 카메라 기능으로는 '파노라마 모드'가 가장 흔해요. 풍경을 말할 때는 '탁 트인 전망'과 비슷하고, '지난 일이 파노라마처럼 스쳐 가다'처럼 기억이 연달아 떠오를 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I switched the camera to panorama mode.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰 카메라 기능을 말할 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use is for the phone camera feature.

phrases.en: Old memories passed by like a panorama.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기억이나 장면이 연달아 떠오를 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for memories or scenes coming one after another.

phrases.example: 산 위에서 탁 트인 전망을 봤어요.
phrases.en: I saw a wide-open view from the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍경이 넓게 보이는 뜻이 비슷해서 일상에서 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning for a wide view, and more common in daily speech.

explain_en: On a camera, '파노라마 모드' is the most common use. For scenery it is close to a wide open view, and it is also used when memories pass by one after another, as in '지난 일이 파노라마처럼 스쳐 가다'.

en: bumper crop; good harvest; good crop

examples.en: Apples had a bumper crop this year, so they are cheap.
The weather is good, so farmers expect a good harvest.
Thanks to the good harvest, the village held a feast.
When cabbage has a bumper crop, prices go down.
Even with a bumper crop, the farmers look gloomy.

examples.ko: 지난해 풍작에 이어 올해도 쌀농사가 잘됐어요.
examples.en: Following last year's bumper crop, rice farming went well this year too.

explain: 반대말은 '흉작'이에요. '풍년'은 농사가 잘된 해를 가리키고, '풍작'은 수확이 많은 것에 초점이 있어요. 풍작이면 값이 내려갈 수 있어서 뉴스에서 가격과 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 올해 농부들이 배 농사에서 풍작을 거뒀어요.
phrases.en: This year farmers got a bumper pear harvest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수확이 많을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when the harvest is large.

phrases.en: Napa cabbage prices fell a lot because of the bumper crop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수확이 많아서 값이 싸질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a big harvest lowers prices.
phrases.en_equiv: prices fall due to a bumper crop

phrases.en: It's a good harvest year, so the village is happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍작은 수확이 많은 것이고, 풍년은 농사가 잘된 해를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 풍작 is the big harvest; 풍년 is the good year overall.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a good harvest year

explain_en: The opposite is '흉작' (poor harvest). '풍년' refers to a year when farming went well, while '풍작' focuses on the large yield. A big harvest can lower prices, so it often appears in the news together with prices.

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 도배를 새로 했어요.
examples.en: I had the walls newly papered before moving.
After wallpapering, there is a smell of paste.

examples.ko: 벽지 값보다 도배 비용이 더 비싸요.
examples.en: The wallpapering cost is higher than the price of the wallpaper.
After the wallpapering was done, the room brightened up.

examples.ko: 도배 기술자가 하루 만에 방을 끝냈어요.
examples.en: The wallpapering worker finished the room in one day.
Mold has formed, so the walls need new wallpaper.

explain: '도배'는 '벽지', '장판'과 함께 집 공사 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 인터넷에서 같은 글을 계속 올리는 것도 '도배'라고 해서, 앞뒤 말을 보고 구분해요.

phrases.en: I wallpapered the room myself over the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '도배'에 '하다'를 붙여 동작으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '하다' to '도배' makes it an action verb.

phrases.en: I left the wallpapering to a professional.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 다른 사람에게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you hand the job to someone else.

phrases.en: When I moved, I redid the wallpaper and the floor covering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 공사에서 함께 자주 말하는 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair often mentioned together in home renovation.

explain_en: '도배' often appears alongside '벽지' and '장판' when talking about home renovation. Posting the same message over and over online is also called '도배', so tell them apart from the context.

examples.en: We rented the whole pension and had fun as a family.

examples.ko: 독채라서 소음 걱정 없이 지낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a standalone house, so you can stay without worrying about noise.
This house is a whole-house jeonse, so it's expensive.
I booked a whole hanok house for our stay.

examples.ko: 독채를 쓰니까 마당도 마음대로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Since we use the whole house, we can use the yard freely too.

examples.ko: 원룸 말고 독채로 이사 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to move into a standalone house instead of a studio.

explain: 다른 사람과 나누지 않고 건물 한 채를 통째로 쓰는 것을 말해요. 방 하나만 빌리는 경우와 비교할 때 써요. 펜션이나 한옥 숙소를 예약할 때 자주 보이는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I booked a pension where we get the whole house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숙소를 고를 때 자주 보이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when choosing accommodation.

phrases.example: 이 집을 우리 가족이 독채로 쓰고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our family uses this whole house by ourselves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물 전체를 혼자 또는 한 팀이 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one person or group has the entire building.

phrases.en: We spent a night in a private hanok house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한옥 숙소에서도 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also common for traditional hanok stays.

explain_en: A whole separate house rented out, as in pensions (독채 펜션) It means using a whole building by yourself without sharing it with others. It's used in contrast with renting just one room. You often see it when booking a pension or hanok stay.

examples.en: I watered the plants with a watering can.
I left the watering can on the balcony.
The watering can is old and its holes are clogged.

examples.ko: 물뿌리개 대신 페트병으로 물을 줘도 돼요.
examples.en: You can water plants with a plastic bottle instead of a watering can.
Water comes out gently from this watering can.
Please fill the watering can with water.

explain: 꽃이나 화분에 물을 줄 때 쓰는 도구예요. 일상에서는 '물조리개'라고도 말해요. 주로 '물뿌리개로 물을 주다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Grandmother waters the flowers with a watering can.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물뿌리개'와 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 물뿌리개, and common in daily speech.

phrases.en: Every morning I water the pots with a watering can.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation.
phrases.en_equiv: to water with a watering can

phrases.en: I filled the watering can with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 주기 전에 준비하는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the preparation before watering.

explain_en: It is the tool used to water flowers and pots. In daily talk it is also called '물조리개'. It is mostly used as '물뿌리개로 물을 주다'.

examples.en: I put a banana and milk in the blender and blended them.
The blender was so loud that the baby woke up.
I blend fruit in the blender to make juice.

examples.ko: 새 믹서를 사고 싶은데 추천해 주세요.
examples.en: I want to buy a new blender, so please recommend one.
Close the blender lid and press the button.
The blender gets louder when you add ice.

explain: 집에서 과일이나 채소를 가는 기계는 '블렌더'보다 '믹서'라고 부르는 일이 더 익숙해요. 보통 '믹서에 갈다', '믹서로 갈다'처럼 '갈다'와 같이 쓰고, 반죽을 섞는 기계와는 달라요.

phrases.en: I made fruit juice with the blender.
phrases.nuance_ko: '믹서'와 같은 뜻이고, 기계라는 느낌을 더해 '믹서기'라고도 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 믹서; adding 기 (machine) is also very common.

phrases.en: I grind tomatoes in the blender to make sauce.
phrases.nuance_ko: '믹서'와 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 믹서.

phrases.en: Every morning I run the blender to make juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계를 켜서 작동시킨다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means turning on and running the machine.

explain_en: For the kitchen machine that grinds fruit or vegetables, Koreans are used to calling it a '믹서' rather than a 'blender'. It usually goes with '갈다' (to grind), as in '믹서에 갈다'.
